q: ____ describes the quantitative relationships among elements in compounds.
e: Composition stoichiometry describes the quantitative relationships among elements in compounds. Stoichiometry is the quantitative bookkeeping of how much of each substance takes part in a reaction.

q: The calculation of molecular mass, relative molecular mass and relative formula mass, calculation of molecular formula and ____, and calculation of percentage composition by mass of a particular element in a compound are included in composition stoichiometry.
e: The calculation of molecular mass, relative molecular mass and relative formula mass, calculation of molecular formula and empirical formula, and calculation of percentage composition by mass of a particular element in a compound are included in composition stoichiometry. Stoichiometry is the quantitative bookkeeping of how much of each substance takes part in a reaction. Composition stoichiometry is about the quantitative ratios of elements inside a compound. The molecular formula gives the actual number of each kind of atom in one molecule.

q: In stoichiometric calculation, the SI unit for the amount of chemical substances is the ____, abbreviated as mol.
e: In stoichiometric calculation, the SI unit for the amount of chemical substances is the mole, abbreviated as mol. The SI base unit for amount of substance is the mole.

q: One mole of a substance is defined as the amount of substance that contains the same number of particles as there are atoms in exactly ____ of pure carbon-12 atom.
e: One mole of a substance is defined as the amount of substance that contains the same number of particles as there are atoms in exactly 12 g of pure carbon-12 atom. The SI base unit for amount of substance is the mole. One mole is the amount that holds as many particles as 12 g of carbon-12, which is 6.02 x 10^23 particles. The mole is defined from 12 g of pure carbon-12, which holds one mole of carbon atoms.

q: One mole of a substance is defined as the amount of substance that contains the same number of particles as there are atoms in exactly 12 g of pure ____ atom.
e: One mole of a substance is defined as the amount of substance that contains the same number of particles as there are atoms in exactly 12 g of pure carbon-12 atom. The SI base unit for amount of substance is the mole. One mole is the amount that holds as many particles as 12 g of carbon-12, which is 6.02 x 10^23 particles.
1 mole = 6.02214179 x 10^23 particles. 1 mole = particles in this chemistry fact.

q: This number is often rounded to $6.02 \times 10^{23}$, and it is called ____.
e: This number is often rounded to 6.02 x 10^23, and it is called Avogadro's number. Avogadro's number is about 6.02 x 10^23 particles in one mole. Avogadro links gas volume at the same T and P to the number of particles, and one mole holds 6.02 x 10^23 of them.

q: The mass of one mole of atoms of a pure element in grams is numerically equal to the ____ of that element in atomic mass units.
e: The mass of one mole of atoms of a pure element in grams is numerically equal to the atomic mass of that element in atomic mass units. One mole is the amount that holds as many particles as 12 g of carbon-12, which is 6.02 x 10^23 particles.

q: The mass of one mole of molecules of a compound in grams is numerically equal to the ____ of that compound.
e: The mass of one mole of molecules of a compound in grams is numerically equal to the molecular mass of that compound. One mole is the amount that holds as many particles as 12 g of carbon-12, which is 6.02 x 10^23 particles.

q: This is called the ____ of the element or compound; its units are gram per mole ($g \text{ mol}^{-1}$) or milligram per millimole ($mg \text{ mmol}^{-1}$).
e: This is called the molar mass of the element or compound. its units are gram per mole (g mol^-1) or milligram per millimole (mg mmol^-1).

q: ____ are salts in which one or more water molecules are chemically combined.
e: Hydrated salts are salts in which one or more water molecules are chemically combined. A hydrated salt has water of crystallisation chemically bound in the crystal, not just mixed in.

q: Some examples of hydrated salts are oxalic acid dihydrate, $(COOH)_2 \cdot 2H_2O$ and ____, $CuSO_4 \cdot 5H_2O$.
e: Some examples of hydrated salts are oxalic acid dihydrate, (COOH)_2 · 2H_2O and copper(II) sulphate pentahydrate, CuSO_4 · 5H_2O. Copper(II) sulphate solution is a common electrolyte, and hydrated CuSO4·5H2O is blue. A hydrated salt has water of crystallisation chemically bound in the crystal, not just mixed in.

q: The water found in crystals is called ____ and it is defined as water that occurs as a constituent of crystalline substances in a definite stoichiometric ratio.
e: The water found in crystals is called water of crystallisation and it is defined as water that occurs as a constituent of crystalline substances in a definite stoichiometric ratio. Water of crystallisation is water locked into a crystal lattice in a definite ratio.

q: Stoichiometry is a part of chemistry which deals with the ____ taking part in a chemical reaction.
e: Stoichiometry is a part of chemistry which deals with the quantities of substances taking part in a chemical reaction. Stoichiometry is the quantitative bookkeeping of how much of each substance takes part in a reaction.
